newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Clark taps U.S. firm for power plant.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Clark taps U.S. firm for power plant.

text.p: The Clark Development Corp said on Tuesday it had signed a joint venture agreement with Polar Energy Inc to build an oil-fired power plant inside the Clark Special Economic Zone in the northern Philippines.
Clark said in a statement the power plant, which will have a minimum 100-megawatt capacity, will be built two years after U.S.-based Polar submits a detailed plan for the $83-million project.

"This project is seen to boost our vision for Clark to become a world-class metropolis. It would assure us of an efficient delivery of power inside the zone even with a rise in demand brought about by an increasing number of commercial, industrial and aviation-related activities," Clark president Romeo David said.
The plant will provide power to residents within the 4,440-hectare main zone and the 30,000-hectare sub-zone, the statement said.
